themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 21 THIS WEEK, a 320% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 5.0 complaints per week (z-score: 7.16), suggesting a sudden shift in TLC vehicle activity or resident frustration in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 21 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 7.16 indicates highly statistically significant spike
320% increase is among the largest proportional spikes in the dataset
reporting_angles: Interview residents about specific complaints: illegal parking, blocking driveways, noise from idling vehicles
Investigate whether a new TLC base or rideshare hub opened recently in or near the district
Contact TLC to see if there's been a surge in vehicle registrations or trip volume in CD 402

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK, a 2,300% spike from the 8-week baseline average of 0.2 per week (z-score: 13.28), indicating rapid expansion of sidewalk/street dining may be triggering resident backlash over noise, waste, or space encroachment.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 13.28 represents one of the highest statistical anomalies in the dataset
2,300% proportional increase suggests a new or sudden expansion of outdoor dining infrastructure
reporting_angles: Map which commercial strips in Sunnyside/Woodside have added or expanded outdoor dining since pandemic restrictions lifted
Interview residents and business owners about the specific complaints: spillover trash, loud patrons, blocked sidewalk access
Check if the city issued new outdoor dining permits or extended the Open Restaurants program in this district recently

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, an 833% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 0.8 per week (z-score: 9.45), suggesting either increased park usage/events or a specific noise source (construction, events, gatherings) that needs investigation.
evidence: 7 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 9.45 indicates highly statistically significant spike
833% increase correlates with seasonal warming and higher park attendance
reporting_angles: Identify which parks in CD 402 (Sunnyside Park, etc.) are generating complaints and via what activity
Check if there are scheduled events, concerts, or gatherings happening in district parks this week
Interview Parks Dept about noise enforcement patrols and hours in community parks

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints skyrocketed to 7 LAST WEEK, a 5,500% spike from the 8-week baseline average of 0.1 per week (z-score: 20.79), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, suggesting either a disease event, pest outbreak, or heat/weather stress affecting street trees.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 20.79 is the single largest statistical anomaly in the entire dataset
5,500% proportional increase suggests a district-wide event rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Investigate what is causing mass tree death: emerging pest (e.g., emerald ash borer, longhorned beetle), disease, drought, or heat stress from recent weather
Contact NYC Parks Urban Forest management and arborists for context on whether this is localized to CD 402 or part of broader citywide pattern
Visit neighborhoods where complaints clustered to document tree conditions and photograph affected areas
Interview residents about when they first noticed decline and whether specific tree species or blocks are affected

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints rose to 23 THIS WEEK, a 52% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 15.1 per week (z-score: 4.47), suggesting either new construction, commercial expansion, or a specific noise-generating business operating above permitted hours.
evidence: 23 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 15.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
52% increase is more modest than other spikes but still statistically significant (z-score: 4.47)
Complements the broader noise trend (residential + park + commercial complaints all elevated this week)
reporting_angles: Identify specific commercial establishments (bars, restaurants, construction sites) generating complaints via 311 geo-data
Cross-reference with DOB permits to see if large-scale renovation or new construction projects ramped up this week
Interview NYPD or DoE noise enforcement about complaint hotspots and whether they've increased patrols
